terms.grammar: verb, third conjugation, deponent, with the ablative
evidence: Cic. Cat. 1.1: abūtēre, Catilīna, patientiā nostrā (Lewis & Short)
terms.comment: Its first sense is to use up or to make full use of (ōtiō, to spend one’s leisure, Cic. Rep. 1.9); the bad sense, to misuse, is as classical. The thing misused is in the ablative.

terms.grammar: phrase: male with ūtor, ūtī, ūsus sum and the ablative
terms.comment: The plain opposite of bene ūtī: of a gift, a chance, one’s time.

phrases.latin: quō ūsque tandem abūtēre, Catilīna, patientiā nostrā?
phrases.english: how long, Catiline, will you go on abusing our patience?
There you go again, misusing words!

sources: Lewis & Short: abutor · Lewis & Short: utor
